issues.display_title: Issue #956: feat(share): Secured Project section in the share modal (#946)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: #946 (R1–R6) · Design: #952 · Decisions: #955 · Design branch: design/secured-published

The Secured Project section in the Share Published Project modal, wired to the real API.

Start from the design branch, but delete its storage layer

design/secured-published already codes this section (src/components/preview/SecuredProjectSection.tsx) and its copy is what #952 approved — keep it. What must NOT come across is src/lib/security/securedProject.ts: it stores the password in plaintext in localStorage, keyed by share key, so the setting is invisible to every other browser. Its own header says MOCK DATA and TODO(integration). Replace it with updateProject.

Copy (PRD §6, matches the design branch)

Section Secured Project · toggle Require password · field Project password · action Save security
On: Viewers need this password before they can open the map.
Off: Anyone with the public link can open this published project.
Near the secured embed links: Anyone with the secured embed link can open the embedded project — only use it in trusted places.

Two fixes to the design branch's version while integrating:

  • the password input is type="text" there; it should be type="password" with a show/hide toggle
  • Save Security → Save security per PRD §6

Build

  • is_secured onto the Project type and isSecured / password onto updateProject in src/actions/projects.ts.
  • Require a non-empty password when turning it on (R3/R4 — no complexity rules, but not empty).
  • Save / saved / failed states in the modal (the design branch has these; keep them).
  • Share Link, Embed Map and Embed to Virtual Tour stay visible as separate sections.
  • Never render the password back from the server — it is write-only; the API returns only is_secured.

Tests

Component tests with fireEvent (this repo has no @testing-library/user-event — do not add it): the toggle renders both helper texts; save is blocked with an empty password while enabling; turning off does not require one; the success and failure states render; the section is absent for a viewer.

Blocked on

D1 (whether secured is its own switch or a value on the visibility setting — changes this UI outright) and the BE schema task.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/956-secured-share-modal, merged in #959, released to main in #962 and deployed (run on 2f0669e).

The Secured Project section is wired to updateProject. src/lib/security/securedProject.ts from the design branch was not carried over — it stored the password in plaintext in localStorage, so the setting was invisible to every other browser. Its copy and state machine were kept; the input became type="password" with a reveal toggle, and the button reads Save security.

is_public became one setting with three values, resolved by projectVisibility() in src/lib/projects/visibility.ts — not in actions/projects.ts, because that file is "use server" and only async server actions may be exported from one. tsc does not catch that; only the build does.

The dashboard menu cannot express three values in two items, so it only moves in the safe direction: a secured project's item reads Make Private, never Make Public. projectActionFailure now reads the body on 400 as well as 403 so the API's validation message reaches the user.

Files: src/actions/projects.ts, src/lib/projects/visibility.ts (new), src/lib/projects/projectActionResult.ts, src/components/preview/SecuredProjectSection.tsx (new), src/components/preview/PreviewShareModal.tsx, src/components/preview/PreviewTopbar.tsx, src/components/dashboard/ProjectViews.tsx.

Commit: 151e411

issues.display_title: Issue #957: feat(viewer): locked project page and unlock flow (#946)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: #946 (R8–R14) · Design: #952 · Decisions: #955 · Design branch: design/secured-published

The locked-project page a visitor sees, and the unlock flow behind it.

The bug to not reproduce

On design/secured-published, src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx calls hydratePersistedState(result.data) before it checks whether the project is secured. Its own comment admits it: "data is hydrated into the store either way". The whole floorplan is already in the browser — and in the network response — before the lock screen renders. Anyone can read it from devtools.

The gate has to be the API refusing to send content, not React declining to mount it. Fetch nothing but metadata until unlocked.

Likewise src/lib/security/accessGate.ts grants access by writing "granted" to localStorage — a visitor can set that themselves. Remembered access must be a grant the API issued and verifies.

Copy (PRD §6)

Title This project is locked · description Enter the project password to view this published MapThru project. · field Project password · button Unlock project · error That password is not correct. Try again. · loading Checking password…

PRD: "It should not feel like an account login page." Keep MapThru branding and a lock icon; no email field, no sign-up link.

Build

  • LockedProjectGate from the design branch, wired to the real unlock endpoint.
  • Add a locked state to the LiveFloorplanResult union in src/actions/projects.ts, alongside the private reason added for #933.
  • Wrong password re-prompts with the error; no retry limit in the UI (R12 — but see D3, the server may throttle, and the UI must render that answer rather than pretend it did not happen).
  • Store the API-issued grant per project and send it on later visits; if it is rejected or missing, show the page again (R13/R14).
  • Both /v/[key] and /embed/[key] go through this.
  • generateMetadata in layout.tsx still emits a share card for a secured project (R7) — but only what D2 rules is safe to expose before unlock.

Tests

Locked renders the gate and not the viewer; a correct password swaps to the map; a wrong one shows the error and allows another attempt; a stored grant skips the prompt; a rejected grant re-prompts; an unsecured project is untouched. Extend src/app/v/[key]/__tests__/metadata.test.ts for the secured card.

Blocked on

D2 (what metadata exists before unlock), D3 (throttling — the UI must show it), D4 (what the grant is), and the BE gate task.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/957-locked-project-page, merged in #960, released in #962 and deployed.

The design branch's bug is not reproduced: it called hydratePersistedState before checking whether the project was secured, so the whole floorplan reached the browser while the password card was on screen. Here the grant goes out with the first request and the API refuses to build the payload without it. A test reproduces the old ordering and fails on it.

Remembered access is the API-issued grant, not the string "granted" in localStorage. A rejected grant is dropped so a later visit does not spend a round trip on it.

locked is a third case everywhere it matters — the result union, generateMetadata, and analytics. Private and locked want opposite metadata treatment: #933 strips a private project's name, R7 keeps a secured one's. Verified in production: map-thru.com/v/<key> on a secured project emits the project's own name in og:title, which only the locked branch does, and carries no canvasData.

A throttled attempt reports as throttled, not as a wrong password — it was never checked against one.

Files: src/app/v/[key]/page.tsx, src/app/v/[key]/layout.tsx, src/components/preview/LockedProjectGate.tsx (new), src/lib/projects/projectGrant.ts (new), src/actions/projects.ts, src/lib/analytics/viewerEvent.ts.

issues.display_title: Issue #958: feat(share): secured embed links, and close the share-link bypass (#946)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: #946 (R15–R17) · Decisions: #955

Secured embed links, and closing the bypass.

R17 is the whole point of this task

"The normal share link cannot be used as a shortcut to embed a secured project." A secured project embedded via the ordinary /embed/{key} URL must still hit the lock — otherwise the password is decorative for anyone who can write an iframe.

On the design branch the "secured" embed link is a ?token= compared against a value in the owner's own localStorage, so it neither travels nor verifies. The token has to be issued and checked by the API (see D4).

Build

  • Embed Map and Embed to Virtual Tour show the secured link when the project is secured, and the ordinary link when it is not (R15/R16/R18).
  • Changing the password must not invalidate embed links already handed out — the embed grant is not derived from the password.
  • The warning near the secured embed links (copy in the modal task) — that link is a bearer credential.
  • Private (#933) and unpublished projects keep their current behaviour untouched (R19/R20).

Tests

Unit tests on the URL builders: secured vs unsecured, embed vs share, and that the plain share key cannot open a secured project's embed. Assert the four states — published / unpublished / private / secured — do not overlap.

Blocked on

D4 (what the embed grant is) and the BE gate task.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/958-secured-embed-links, merged in #961, released in #962 and deployed.

R17 was mostly already true once the gate moved into the API: /embed/{key} without a grant meets the lock exactly as /v/{key} does. What this added is the deliberate exception — both embed links carry the owner's grant — and the test pinning that the share link never gets one.

The grant is appended by withProjectGrant, not concatenated at the call site: the result is interpolated into an iframe src, so it is encoded once by the same function that encodes the key. The design branch built its ?token= by string addition.

If the grant cannot be minted the links stay plain and both sections say why — a plain link meets the password page, which is the correct failure.

Lint caught a real bug while integrating: the effect set state synchronously. Fixing it by deriving the value also closed an edge where one project's grant could be displayed against another.

Known gap: an embed grant cannot be revoked. Rotating a leaked link needs a version counter on the project row; marked in the backend code.

Files: src/lib/preview/publish.ts, src/components/preview/PreviewShareModal.tsx, src/actions/projects.ts.

issues.display_title: Issue #955: [Decision] Secured Published Project (#946) — 5 answers needed before the gate is written
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

PRD: #946 · Design: #952 (In review on board #106) · Design branch: design/secured-published

Code review of #946 says the feature is buildable, but five answers are needed before anyone writes the gate. Each states the choice and its cost; none needs engineering input to decide.

D1 — How does secured compose with is_public? (blocking)

is_public shipped this week (#933/#940). A published project can already be public or private. secured would be a third thing.

Option Meaning Cost
A. A third axis — published × public/private × secured A private project can also carry a password Every gate has to evaluate both, and "private + secured" needs a defined answer
B. Secured replaces private — one visibility setting with three values: public / secured / private Simpler to explain and to build; one setting, one answer Changes the meaning of the toggle just shipped

Recommendation: B. Owners think in one question — "who can open this link?" — and three mutually exclusive answers are easier to get right than two overlapping switches. A is more code in the one place where a mistake leaks a project.

D2 — R7 wants metadata visible, R8 wants content hidden. Which response carries which? (blocking)

GET /v1/live/:key returns the entire floorplan in one response. It cannot both show a share card and withhold the map.

Option Cost
A. Split the response — a small metadata-only payload before unlock, the full one after Medium. Clean, and the locked page gets a real title
B. Metadata-only endpoint alongside the existing one Similar, but a second public route to keep gated correctly
C. Drop R7 — a secured project shares as a generic MapThru card Free

Recommendation: A.

D3 — R12 says unlimited password attempts. Is that really the ruling? (blocking)

R12: "There is no limit on wrong password attempts." R4: no complexity rules. The API has no rate limiting anywhere. Together that is an unthrottled online guessing oracle against a password the owner was told needs no complexity — and repeated bcrypt calls on an anonymous route are also a CPU-exhaustion surface.

Option Cost
A. Keep R12, add a slowdown that is not a lockout — per-IP throttle after N wrong attempts, never a permanent block Small. Honours the intent (nobody gets locked out) without leaving the door open
B. Keep R12 literally, no throttle Free, and the feature does not really protect anything
C. Add a real attempt limit Contradicts R12 as written

Recommendation: A. R12's purpose reads as "a visitor must never be locked out"; a throttle satisfies that, an open oracle is not what it was asking for.

D4 — What is the unlock grant, given passwords can change?

"Changing the password must not break existing secured embed links" means the grant cannot be derived from the password. Nothing in the API covers an anonymous, project-scoped grant (models.OTP is keyed to a user).

Option Cost
A. A signed, project-scoped token the API issues on correct password and verifies thereafter Small — HS256 sign/verify already exists, needs its own claims
B. An opaque per-project embed key stored on the project, rotated only on request Simple, but one long-lived secret in URLs

Recommendation: A for visitor access, B for the embed link — they are different lifetimes.

D5 — Is GET /v1/live/:key/file gated?

That route serves the OG share card to crawlers carrying nothing. Gate it and the share card disappears; leave it open and floor images are readable by filename.

Recommendation: gate everything except the share-card image itself, once D2 splits metadata from content.

Two things that are not decisions, just facts to know

The design branch does not lock anything. design/secured-published stores the password in plaintext in localStorage and hydrates the whole floorplan before showing the lock screen. Its author marked it MOCK DATA and TODO(integration). It is a UI reference — the copy and states are good and should be kept; src/lib/security/ must be deleted, not merged.

A gate on /v1/live/:key alone is not a gate. GET /v1/floorplan/:id is route-public and returns the identical payload by UUID — and that UUID is in the editor URL and in localStorage. There are three public read paths, and any gate belongs where they converge.

Tasks are filed and will be built in this order once D1–D3 are answered: BE schema → BE gate → FE modal → FE locked page → FE embed links.

ANSWERED — and what was built

D1 → B. One visibility setting, three mutually exclusive values: public / secured / private. is_public is still written in lockstep for one release so a rollback reads the right value.

D2 → A. Split response. GET /v1/live/:key answers 401 for a locked project carrying the project name and nothing else; the floorplan payload is never built.

D3 → A. Throttle, not lockout. POST /v1/live/:key/unlock is rate limited per IP and per project using the limiter already in the pinned Fiber module — no new dependency. The window always expires; nobody is barred.

D4 → answered in code, and the shape differs from the recommendation above. Rather than a signed token plus an opaque column, both grants are the same signed primitive with different lifetimes: the visitor's expires in 7 days, the embed one has no expiry and no iat, which makes it a pure function of the secret and the project — the same string every time it is minted, so a link already pasted into a customer's tour never changes and survives a password change (R16). That delivers option B's properties with no new column.

What it does not deliver is revocation. A leaked embed link cannot be rotated without a version counter on the project row. Flagged in utils.GrantTypeEmbed with the upgrade path. Worth adding the first time an owner asks.

D5 → gated, which is the opposite of the recommendation above. GET /v1/live/:key/file is closed for a secured project without a grant, because that image is a render of the floorplan and therefore content. R7 still holds: the project name comes back in the 401, and the share card falls to the brand image — the same path a private project already used. An unlocked visitor still gets the images, because that route accepts a grant.

One thing the review above got wrong

It claimed the direct MinIO URLs in buildFloorplanResponse bypass the gate. They do not. MINIO_PUBLIC_READ is unset, so ObjectURL returns a presigned URL that expires in 24 hours, and no URL of any kind is emitted for a locked project — the payload is never built. The residual is that an unlocked visitor holds image URLs valid for 24 hours; if MINIO_PUBLIC_READ is ever turned on, those become permanent.

Shipped

API-GO #175 → main, migration applied and verified on production (525 rows backfilled, 0 left). Frontend #962 → main, deployed. Verified end to end on map-thru.com.

issues.display_title: Issue #963: Plot labels vanish at site zoom: size the dot/label switch to the object, not the zoom (#930)
issues.main_description_html:
Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Source: #930 (AC1 + the map half of AC3) · Scope note: #939 · Design: #931 · Live subject: https://map-thru.com/v/HtRJfJxe

AC2 (spatial hotspots inside the 360 viewer) is descoped — see #939 for why, and the instruction of 2026-09-08.

The bug, stated exactly

The plots already exist and already render. Someone added them by hand to "Kuwait (Sample)": seven manual Areas — Plot 101 … Plot 107 — each linked to an Information record that carries the name (labelType: "icon", labelIcon: "location-dot"). Search finds all seven, selecting one opens its info card and tints the polygon. AC1's rendering and AC3's map half need no new code.

What is broken is that the labels are invisible at every zoom where the site is readable.

Zoom What the visitor sees
Default landing view (Overview, < 16.25) Nothing — PreviewOverlay.tsx:1120 is {!outdoor && <MapObjectMarkers …>}, so the whole overlay is unmounted
Indoor, whole site in frame All seven present in the DOM, every one a 10×10 dot — DOT_ZOOM = 19 (MapObjectMarkers.tsx:26,289)
Past zoom 19 Labels draw, but only one or two plots fit on screen

Measured on the live page: at the zoom the visitor lands on after entering the building, Plot 101's own footprint spans ~340 screen px and it is still drawn as a 10 px dot. That is the whole client-visible failure.

Root cause

DOT_ZOOM is a proxy for "these objects are too small to carry a label". It is a single global zoom number, so it cannot tell a 25 m land parcel from a 2 m parking stall — and this project has 73 parking stalls, so the proxy cannot simply be lowered. #460 raised it 18 → 19 for exactly that reason.

Replace the proxy with the measurement it stands for: an object whose own footprint is large on screen keeps its label, whatever the zoom.

Build

1. Per-marker dot decision (MapObjectMarkers.tsx, object-markers.ts)

  • MarkerAnchor gains extentHalf?: { dx, dy } — the plan-unit half-extent of an area's bounding box, set for area markers (points, panos, access, safety and doors have no footprint and keep the global rule).
  • mercRef projects the two box diagonals the same way the closed-room logo box already does (corner(±1)) — one diagonal alone crosses zero as the floor rotates.
  • Per frame: dotThis = zoom < DOT_ZOOM && projectedSpan < LABEL_SPAN_PX. Keep DOT_ZOOM as the upper bound so nothing that labels today stops labelling.
  • sizeRef's cache key must use the per-marker flag, not the global one.

LABEL_SPAN_PX ≈ 120 (on-screen diagonal). At that value the Kuwait plots (340–545 px) label immediately, the parking stalls (~29 px) stay dots, and a shopping-mall tenant at zoom 18 (~46 px) is unchanged — so imported Mappedin projects see no difference below zoom 19.

2. Overview shows site-scale labels only (PreviewOverlay.tsx)

Mount MapObjectMarkers in Overview too, with a new siteScaleOnly prop that hides every marker failing the same size test. One rule, two mount conditions: Overview gains the plot names and gains nothing else — a mall's tenants are ~20 px there and stay hidden, so no project can turn Overview into label soup.

Do not change Editor3DMapView's call site in this task.

Acceptance

  • Landing on /v/HtRJfJxe shows the seven plot names without touching a control
  • Entering the building keeps them; they do not blink out in the 16.75–19 band
  • Parking stalls stay dots below zoom 19 and label at 19 exactly as today
  • No change to any project with no site-scale areas

Tests

MapObjectMarkers.test.tsx already fakes the projection matrix and asserts the dot/full split — extend it: an area with a large extentHalf renders its full label below DOT_ZOOM; one with a small extentHalf stays a dot; siteScaleOnly hides the small one entirely. Unit-test the anchor's extentHalf from a known boundary ring in object-markers.

Out of scope

  • AC2, the 360 viewer hotspots (#939 §AC2 — descoped)
  • Badge styling (#931 is still Overview on Project #106; this ships in the existing marker pill and can be re-skinned later)
  • Any new "plot" entity or schema — a plot is a manual Area plus an Information record, which is what the client already built

RESULT

Implemented on feature/963-plot-label-site-scale, commit 99d4756. Not pushed — awaiting approval.

An area now carries its own footprint (MarkerAnchor.extentHalf, the plan-unit half-extent of its bounding box). The overlay projects it each frame with the same ±diagonal pair the closed-room logo box uses, and anything reaching LABEL_REACH_PX around its own label keeps that label whatever the zoom. DOT_ZOOM stays the upper bound, so nothing that labels today stops labelling. Point-like kinds — points, panoramas, access, safety, doors — have no footprint and keep the flat rule.

PreviewOverlay mounts the overlay in Overview too, restricted by the same test via siteScaleOnly. That flag is what makes it safe: the parcels clear the bar there, the 2 097 panorama markers do not, so the landing view gains the plot names and nothing else.

The threshold is measured, not guessed — and 120 was wrong

The task body proposed LABEL_SPAN_PX ≈ 120. That was derived from screen distances between plot anchors, but the code measures anchor-to-farthest-corner, which is roughly half that. Instrumented the running page and read the real values at the Overview landing camera:

reach (px)
The Gate Mall 146
plots 101 / 103 / 107 92 / 90 / 88
plot 104 69
cricket ground 62
largest parking lot 61
plots 102 / 106 / 105 58 / 54 / 51
— bar at 40 —
OGAL-C 39
2nd / 3rd parking lot 37 / 36
the mosque 30
median parking stall 8

50 was tried first and sat 2% above the smallest parcel; a camera nudge dropped three plots out, which is what the flapping in early runs was. 40 sits in the gap with 28% clearance and still excludes 71 of the 72 stalls — the one it admits is a genuinely large lot.

What this does and does not deliver

Verified against the live project through the local dev server:

  • Landing view (Overview): Plot 101, 103, 104, 107 named, plus the cricket ground, the large parking lot and The Gate Mall. Before: nothing at all.
  • After entering the building: plots stay named through the 16.75–19 band where they used to be dots. 666 panoramas and 49 stalls stay dots; the large lot labels.

Four of the seven plots draw at the far-out view, not all seven. The other three are eligible and lose to ordinary declutter: their anchors are 36 px apart and the marker pill is ~70 px wide, so seven of them cannot coexist at that zoom. That is geometry, not a gate — they appear as the visitor zooms. Sizing a badge that fits is #931, still unstarted on Project #106.

Screenshots: .playwright-mcp/screenshot/930-live-{default,indoor}.png (before) and 963-after-{overview,indoor}.png (after).

Checks

pnpm exec vitest run — 233 files, 2 241 passed, 3 skipped. pnpm lint — 0 errors (13 pre-existing warnings, all in gitignored demo scenarios). tsc --noEmit clean.

Tests added: five in MapObjectMarkers.test.tsx (large object labels below DOT_ZOOM; small one stays a dot; small one still labels past DOT_ZOOM; siteScaleOnly keeps the large one and hides the small one entirely; the size test still answers past DOT_ZOOM, which caught a real bug — siteScale was initially gated on dot, so siteScaleOnly at close zoom would have hidden everything). Three in object-markers.test.ts for extentHalf, including a degenerate ring.

Files: src/lib/map/object-markers.ts, src/components/editor/map-markers/MapObjectMarkers.tsx, src/components/editor/PreviewOverlay.tsx + the two test files.

Not touched: Editor3DMapView's call site, per the task. AC2 remains descoped.

Demo

.playwright-mcp/demo/963/video-963-plot-labels.mp4 — 1920×1080, 60 fps, 2:18, GPU (Tesla P4 / ANGLE Vulkan).

Recorded from the worktree against :6061. The before half is production, not a mock: map-thru.com/v/HtRJfJxe still serves the old build, so the video is the same live project and the same share link on both sides, with the same landing camera.

Read-only throughout — both halves open a public /v/ link and never sign in, publish or edit, so unlike the #946 scenario nothing here touches the database.

What the scenario asserts, with the numbers it printed:

plots in frame labelled dots panorama dots drawn
production, landing view 0 (overlay unmounted) 0 0 0
production, inside 6 0 6 685
fixed, landing view 6 5 0 0
fixed, inside 6 4 0 685

The middle row is the point: on production every plot is on the page and every one is a 10 px dot. The bug was never "the labels are missing".

The last column is the guard against overcorrecting — siteScaleOnly draws the parcel names in Overview and no panorama dots, and indoors all 685 come back as dots while the plots stay named. The scenario fails if either stops being true.

Six of seven, not seven: the landing camera puts one plot off screen, and of the six on screen the closest pair loses to declutter (~36 px between anchors, ~70 px pill). Filmed as it is rather than framed to hide it — the badge that would fit more is #931.

RESULT 2 — the labels now actually float (commit 98263bb)

The first commit fixed whether the label draws. It still drew flat on the ground, which is not what #930 asked for: the client's words are "floating labels above a few land parcels", the issue title is "Floating Plot Labels", and #931 AC2 is "define display scaling and elevation behavior".

A plot is a manual Area with no type, so onClosed was false and alt = h — the level base height. The parcel's own slab top is baseH + area.height (0.2) × wallH ≈ 0.3 m higher, so the label sat below the surface it names. That is the same failure the closed-room branch immediately beside it already guards against, in its own words: "would otherwise sit at the floor, buried inside the solid mass". The guard just never covered extruded pads.

Why the lift is in screen px, not metres

This was the real decision, and the obvious implementation is wrong twice over:

approach at Overview (~z16) at z19
ride to the slab's own top (0.3 m) ≈ 2 px — invisible ≈ 17 px
a height that reads at Overview (4 m) ≈ 28 px ≈ 224 px off the parcel
constant 28 screen px 28 px 28 px

A metre is ~7 px at zoom 16 and ~56 px at 19, so any fixed world height is either invisible or absurd depending where you look from. A constant screen offset is what a floating badge is — the same clearance at every zoom, sitting off the outline rather than on top of it, which is the other half of #931 AC2 ("readable across zoom levels without obscuring parcel outlines").

Scope

Floats only a pad — a standalone Area beside the building (manual, the #839/#884 flag) — and only while it draws a full label. A room's label belongs on its own floor and is untouched; a dot has nothing to float over.

Deliberately not gated on the size rule from the first commit: that is only true below DOT_ZOOM, so the label would have dropped back onto the parcel the moment the visitor crossed zoom 19.

Declutter now reserves the box where the pill is drawn rather than at the anchor. screenPosRef still publishes the anchor — #850's readers want where the object is, not where its label hovers.

LABEL_FLOAT_PX = 28 is provisional and marked ponytail:. #931 owns the badge and its elevation; this is one constant to retune.

Checks

233 files, 2 243 passed, 3 skipped. Lint 0 errors, tsc --noEmit clean.

Four tests added: a pad's label is drawn 28 px above its object; the lift is identical at zoom 17 and 21 (the regression the DOT_ZOOM gating would have caused); a room's label stays on its anchor; a dot does not float.

Verified on the live project — 963-float-overview.png and 963-float-indoor.png. The plot names hover clear of their parcels on both, while "The Gate Mall", a closed room rather than a pad, stays on its massing exactly as before.

The demo video predates this commit and shows the ground-anchored version; worth re-recording before this goes for review.

Deployed

PR #968 → development (07:27), PR #969 → main (07:28), Deploy run 34199494079 success 07:30:30.

development was level with main beforehand, so the release carried exactly the two #963 commits and nothing else.

Verified on production immediately after, same URL the client uses — https://map-thru.com/v/HtRJfJxe, landing view, no interaction:

Plot 101 = label @ y293      Plot 105 = hidden
Plot 103 = label @ y323      Plot 106 = hidden
Plot 104 = label @ y370      panorama dots drawn = 0
Plot 107 = label @ y364

Four names on the view the share link opens, where before the deploy there were none. Every y is 28 px above its own anchor — the float is live. No panorama dots in Overview, so siteScaleOnly is holding in production.

Screenshot: .playwright-mcp/screenshot/963-prod-after-deploy.png.

issues.display_title: Issue #972: feat(events): draft/published flag per Event Highlight (#935)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-935-event-draft.mp4

Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Reported: #935

The report was not the bug

#935 shows the Mappedin import modal reading Event 0. That is correct behaviour: a Mappedin MVF zip carries no events at all — they are a separate CMS entity served by GET api-gateway.mappedin.com/public/1/event/{venue}, outside the export. Confirmed against the live Square One bundle.

The real gap sat elsewhere. Event Highlights had no draft state. A published project reads its Events straight off the live row — publishing only flips status, there is no snapshot in between — so every Event went public on the next 2-second autosave, half-written or not.

Build

  • published?: boolean on EventHighlight. The rule is published !== false: an Event with the field absent predates this change and was already public, so reading absence as a draft would empty the Event panel of every live map on deploy.
  • New Events are created published: false. The safe state is the one that has to be chosen.
  • Visibility control on the modal's Basic tab, the same segmented pair as Open Type — two exclusive choices with their consequence on screen.
  • Draft badge on the sidebar row. The editor keeps drafts listed, the way it already keeps expired Events for review.
  • Filtering happens in visitorEvents(), the single seam /preview, /v/{key} and /embed all pass through.

Tests

Unit tests on the flag rule: explicit false hidden, true and absent both visible. Plus an end-to-end probe against a scratch project — default Draft, badge renders, the flag survives save + reload, visitor count 0 while drafted and 1 once published.

Depends on

The API task, which must ship first — the client-side filter is UX, not the control.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/935-event-publish-toggle, merged in #966, released in #967 and deployed.

The design started somewhere else and was wrong. The first plan was a dedicated Event CRUD API, on the premise that events needed to go live without republishing. Research killed it: there is no publish snapshot anywhere — /v1/live/{key} reads the same project row the editor writes — so that property already existed. A separate table would have bought nothing and cost a manual production migration, a cross-resource cascade for place.infoId, and a second viewer fetch that would have to reproduce the grant/lock gate and the photo-URL rewrite.

What was actually missing was draft state, which is one field.

The rule is implemented twice, in TypeScript and in Go, so the two were checked against each other on every JSON value the field can hold — absent, null, true, false, 0, 1, "false", "", []. They agree on all nine.

Adversarial review (four lenses, verified independently) left one finding standing: an Event photo is an ordinary project file, so it stays listed in uploadedFiles and is fetchable by name from a published project. The leak is enumerable, not merely guessable. The Draft hint was reworded to promise only what the read path delivers — "kept off the visitor's event panel and map" — rather than claiming nobody else can reach it. Closing it needs the photo names filtered out of uploadedFiles in the same pass, or per-file gating; either is a separate task.

Verified on production: the new UI string is present in the chunks served from the prod host, and pm2 restarted.

issues.display_title: Issue #965: fix(add-panorama): corner resize handles on the alignment overlay, drop the scale slider (#964)
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-965-corner-resize.mp4

Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Feedback: #964

The Scale control in Apply Based on Location (Add Panorama, Modal 2) is an <input type="range" min={0.25} max={3}>. It bottoms out at 300%, and the reporter's screenshot shows the bar pinned at the ceiling with the dot cloud still too small for the building. A progress bar is also the wrong affordance here: the user is georeferencing a dot cloud against a floor plan, and the thing they want to grab is the overlay itself.

Build

  • Delete the scale slider from AlignmentControls. The Opacity slider stays — it has a real 0.2–1 range and is not what the feedback is about.
  • Resize handles at the four corners of the dashed overlay box in ApplyLocationModal, dragged to scale the whole rigid dot group.
  • Unlimited upward. No max. Only a small positive floor so scale can never reach 0 or go negative (a zero scale collapses the box to a point with nothing left to grab, and the counter-transform on the dots divides by it).
  • Scale stays uniform — AlignmentTransform carries one scale, and layout() fits the dots with one uniform pixel scale on purpose. No per-axis stretch, at any corner.
  • Handles keep a constant screen size at any scale and camera zoom, the same way the marker dots do via counterTransform.
  • A handle drag must not also trigger the whole-layer group drag on the parent box, and must not disturb the per-pin overrides (#276).
  • Correct under rotation, both flips, and camera zoom (cam.k) — the same three things invertAlignmentDelta already has to survive.
  • Keep a numeric scale readout, as plain text rather than a bar.

Keyboard

The deleted <input type="range"> was keyboard-operable, and §15 of the spec requires the alignment controls be reachable by keyboard — RotateKnob carries that note. Whatever replaces it must keep scale changeable without a pointer.

Tests

Pure helper in types.ts for the corner→scale math, unit-tested next to invertAlignmentDelta:

  • a corner drag under rotation / flipX / flipY / cam.k ≠ 1 lands on the scale the cursor implies
  • scale is floored, never zero or negative, and has no upper bound (a far drag reaches 10×+)
  • the anchor point the design fixes stays fixed across the resize
  • overlayOffset output is unchanged for an untouched transform — the Apply projection must not shift

Out of scope

Per-axis stretch, edge (non-corner) handles, and any change to Opacity, Rotate, Flip, Move or Reset.

Added on request: rotate by handle

Same treatment for Rotate, asked for while the resize work was in review. A rotate handle on a short stalk off the overlay's top edge, so the layer is turned by grabbing it rather than only through the knob.

  • Centre pivot, like the corner handles — a rotate writes nothing but rotation, so overlayOffset, handleApply and the per-pin overrides are untouched.
  • Shift snaps to 15°, snapping the resulting angle rather than the swept delta, so it lands on a true 0/90/180 and an imported plan can be squared to the building.
  • No flip correction, deliberately: the overlay renders as R(θ)·S — rotation outside the flip — so a mirrored layer already follows the cursor and a sign term would break it.
  • The knob stays. It has no ceiling to remove and it is the keyboard route §15 requires; the handle is aria-hidden, one control per value.

Unit tests on rotationFromHandle next to the scale ones: sweep, both flips, camera independence, idempotence, Shift snapping, wrap to (-180, 180], and that the centre does not move.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/965-overlay-corner-resize, merged in #970, released in #971 and deployed.

Scale. Four corner handles on the dashed box, no upper bound. The anchor is the box centre, not the opposite corner the design-tool convention would pick — the centre is already the pivot rotate() and both Flip buttons turn about, it is the dot cloud's own centroid (layout() centres the fitted group on 0.5, 0.5 and insets it by PAD, so the corners are empty padding), and it is the only point whose screen position carries no scale term. So a resize writes nothing but scale, and R5 — do not disturb the Apply projection — holds by construction rather than by test.

scaleFromHandle projects the pointer onto the centre→corner diagonal instead of measuring its distance. One uniform scale, rigid dot group, so the perpendicular component has nothing to drive; a radial measure would grow the box on sideways motion. It is the exact inverse of overlayOffset's corner term, and the tests assert against that helper directly, so drift fails there rather than silently misplacing panoramas.

The range became a number field, not nothing. A range needs a maximum and the maximum was the problem. It is the readout, the keyboard route §15 asks for, and the only way up once a large scale has pushed the handles off the stage. It holds a typing draft keyed to the scale it was typed against — a controlled field that clamps every keystroke rewrites the leading 1 of 1200 as 5, and the draft retires itself the moment the scale changes from anywhere else, so Reset or a floor switch cannot leave a stale number on screen.

Rotate (added on request, same branch): a handle on a stalk off the top edge, centre pivot, Shift snapping to 15°. It snaps the resulting angle rather than the swept delta, so it lands on a true 0/90/180. rotationFromHandle carries no flip term on purpose — the overlay renders as R(θ)·S, rotation outside the flip, so a point's screen angle is θ + angle(S·p) and its derivative in θ is 1 whichever way S mirrors. A sign correction would have broken the flipped case.

Three things the 3× ceiling was hiding, all found by review or by measuring in a browser rather than by the ticket:

  • Opacity sat on the transformed div, so the new handles faded to 20% with the layer they resize. Moved to an inner wrapper.
  • The connection lines and the frame rendered as slabs at high scale. Both take vectorEffect="non-scaling-stroke" now. The frame had to leave its CSS border to get there — a used border-width is floored to a whole pixel, so counter-scaling stops working at 1px, and a browser probe caught 2/scale still painting a 19px ribbon at 12×.
  • clampScale keeps 0, negative, NaN and Infinity out of scale, which counter and invertAlignmentDelta both divide by.

Verified beyond the unit tests. Driven in a real browser against the running app: handles hold 24 screen px from 0.1× to 8×, the grabbed handle ends 0.00 px from the cursor, the box centre moves 0.00 px across both a resize and a 60° rotate, the group drag never fires during a handle drag, dragging past the centre clamps at MIN_SCALE, and Shift snaps to 90°. overlayCamera.test.ts and invertAlignmentDelta.test.ts pass untouched.

Known gap, not fixed. A corner sits 322·scale·cam.k px from the centre and the stage is overflow-hidden, so the handles leave it past ~2× — sooner when the layer is rotated, which swings a corner onto the short axis. Measured in a browser and commented at the call site. Zooming the map out brings them back and the percentage field reaches any value, so the gesture is not a dead end, but a handle-only resize would cap lower than the slider it replaced. Clamping the handles along their diagonal would close it; it needs a grab-offset so the first move does not jump the scale, which is why it is not in this change.

Files: src/components/editor/add-panorama/types.ts, ApplyLocationModal.tsx, AlignmentControls.tsx, plus __tests__/scaleFromHandle.test.ts, __tests__/rotationFromHandle.test.ts, __tests__/AlignmentControls.test.tsx.
